steps.goal: Implement normalize(text) in src/normalize.py: fold full-width ASCII (U+FF01-U+FF5E) to half-width, fold the ideographic space (U+3000) to a normal space, lowercase ASCII letters only, collapse every run of whitespace to a single space, and strip leading and trailing whitespace. Reject a non-str argument rather than coercing it. Characters outside those rules -- Japanese text in particular -- pass through unchanged.

invariants: idempotent: normalize(normalize(t)) == normalize(t) for every str t
only ASCII letters are case-folded; characters outside U+FF01-U+FF5E and U+3000 are returned unchanged

acceptance.then: the result is exactly '日本語 テスト'
the result is exactly '' rather than a single space

steps.goal: Implement tokenize(text) in src/tokenizer.py. It must normalise the input by calling normalize() from src.normalize -- do not reimplement any of that folding here -- and then split the normalised text on single spaces, returning the resulting tokens. A normalised string never has leading, trailing or repeated spaces, so no empty token can occur.

invariants: no token is the empty string
tokenize(t) equals normalize(t).split(chr(32)) for every str t that normalises to a non-empty string

acceptance.then: the result is exactly ['日本語', 'テスト']
the result is exactly [] rather than ['']
TypeError is raised, propagated from normalize

steps.goal: Implement token_counts(text) in src/counts.py using tokenize() from src.tokenizer. The required algorithm is exactly this: start with an empty dict, then iterate the list returned by tokenize(text) in order, and for each token do `d[token] = d.get(token, 0) + 1`. Return that dict. Do not deduplicate or reorder the token list before counting -- every occurrence of every token, including repeats, must go through the increment step. Do not sort the keys, and do not use collections.Counter and then rebuild or reorder its result -- a plain dict built by the increment loop above already has keys in order of first occurrence (Python dicts preserve insertion order, and a key's position is fixed the first time it is inserted, not touched by later increments) and already has correct totals (every token increments its own key once per occurrence). Any extra sorting, deduplication, or Counter-based post-processing step is not needed and will break one of the two invariants below.

invariants: the sum of the values equals len(tokenize(text))
keys appear in order of first occurrence in tokenize(text)
no deduplication happens before counting: a token occurring k times in tokenize(text) contributes k to its own count
no sorting or reordering happens after counting: key order is exactly insertion order from the counting loop, not alphabetical or any other derived order

acceptance.then: TypeError is raised, propagated from tokenize
